claims.behaviour: The default methods isStructureAvailableToUser(user), isCreateStructureAllowed(user), isSynchronizationAllowed(user), isAutomationAccessAllowed(user) and isManageGlobalSavedColumnsAllowed(user) each return exactly what isAllowed returns for, respectively, CoreAppPermissions.USE, CREATE_STRUCTURE, SYNCHRONIZATION, AUTOMATION and MANAGE_GLOBAL_SAVED_COLUMNS with the same user (null passed through unchanged). A stub implementing only isAllowed observes one call per default method with that permission.

The default methods isAuthenticated(), isAdmin(), isSystemAdmin(), getAvailableGroupsForCurrentUser() and getI18n() take the user from the helper's own getUser() (not from StructureAuth): isAuthenticated() is true exactly when getUser() is non-null, and the others delegate to isAdmin(user), isSystemAdmin(user), getAvailableGroups(user) and getI18n(user) with that user, returning their result unchanged.

The defaults getIssueError(Long, boolean), getIssueError(Issue, boolean), getIssueError(Issue, boolean, boolean) and isStructureAvailableToCurrentUser() use the current user from StructureAuth.getUser(). getIssueError(Issue, checkEdit) delegates to the four-argument form with the project-enablement check set to false; getIssueError(Issue, checkEdit, checkProject) passes both flags through.
The default getConfigurationScopeQuery() returns getConfiguration().getConfigurationScopeQuery() unchanged, including null.

In the plugin's implementation getIssueError(Issue, checkEdit, checkProject, user) returns StructureErrors.ITEM_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE for a null issue; otherwise, unless security is overridden in StructureAuth, it checks in order: Browse Projects permission on the issue (failure gives ITEM_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE), then, only if checkProject is true, that the issue's project is enabled in the configuration (failure gives PROJECT_NOT_ENABLED_FOR_STRUCTURE), then, only if checkEdit is true, that Jira reports the issue editable by the user (failure gives ITEM_EDIT_DENIED). It returns null when all applicable checks pass, and always null for a non-null issue when security is overridden.

In the plugin's implementation getIssueError(Long id, checkEdit, user) returns ITEM_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE for a null id or an id with no issue, delegates to the issue form without the project-enablement check otherwise, and returns a Jira data-access error (not an exception) when reading the issue fails.

In the plugin's implementation isAdmin(null) and isSystemAdmin(null) are false; isViewCreationAllowed(null) is false and otherwise equals isStructureAvailableToUser(user); isViewSharingAllowed additionally requires the global 'create shared objects' permission; hasPermission with a null issue or null project, isIssueEditable(null, user) and isProjectStructuredForCurrentUser(null) are all false.

In the plugin's implementation getAvailableGroups(null) returns an empty list; for a Jira administrator (or when the setting structure.permissions.allowAllUserGroups is on) it returns all Jira groups, otherwise only the user's own groups. Every call returns a new mutable list; getAvailableRoles() likewise returns a new mutable list of all project roles.

In the plugin's implementation the comparator from getStructureComparator(user) treats the same instance as equal, sorts null structures after all non-null ones, treats a null name as the empty string, and otherwise orders by name with a collator for the user's locale.

In the plugin's implementation getIssue(long) and getIssue(String) return the issue without any permission check, or null when it does not exist; any exception thrown while reading it is logged and null is returned.

In the plugin's implementation filterInvisibleProjects does nothing for null or empty input; otherwise it adds to the collector each project ID that does not exist or cannot be read, and, when the override flag is false, each project the user may not browse. Visible projects are never added.

The constructor stores its four arguments as given (no copying, no validation, even a null spec is accepted); getAttributeSpec(), getRowId(), getItemId() and getCause() return them unchanged, with null for absent row, item and cause.

toString() is 'problem:' followed by the spec's toString, then ':row=' and the row ID if the row is non-null, then ':item=' and the item identity's toString if non-null, then ':' and the cause's getMessage() if a cause is present (the text 'null' when the cause has no message). Examples: spec key:text alone gives 'problem:key:text'; row 7, item identity with toString 'com.example:t/10' and cause message 'boom' give 'problem:key:text:row=7:item=com.example:t/10:boom'; row 7 with a message-less cause gives 'problem:key:text:row=7:null'.
AttributeErrorInfo does not override equals or hashCode: two instances with equal contents are not equal.

Both public constructors throw IllegalArgumentException when the ID is null, empty or whitespace-only (message 'attribute id must not be empty'), longer than 190 characters ('attribute id must not be longer than 190 chars'; exactly 190 is accepted), or contains a colon ('attribute id must not contain colon'), and when the format is null ('attribute format must not be null'). The ID checks are made before the format check.

The three-argument constructor rejects invalid parameters with IllegalArgumentException: a null key ('null key'), a non-string key ('non-string key: ' plus the key), a null value at any depth ('null value'), or a value that is not a String, Integer, Long, Double, Boolean, List or Map (message starts 'invalid value type: ' plus the class name, e.g. for a Float). Nested lists and maps are checked recursively, and nested maps must have string keys.

The three-argument constructor deep-copies the given map: later changes to the caller's map or its nested lists and maps do not affect the spec. JSON library arrays and objects among the values are converted to lists and maps. A null or empty map gives empty parameters, so new AttributeSpec(id, f, null) and new AttributeSpec(id, f, emptyMap) both equal new AttributeSpec(id, f).

On construction, top-level parameters whose value is null, Boolean false, a Long 0, an empty List, an empty Map, or an Integer equal to the parameter's default are dropped. The Integer default is 0, except -1 for 'depth' and 'level' of the attribute with ID 'aggregation-parent', and 1 for 'fromdepth' and 'fromLevel' of the attributes 'aggregation-join' and 'aggregation-array' (for those, an Integer 0 is kept). Double 0.0 and the empty string are not dropped. Example: params {b:false, x:1, z:0L, l:[]} give a spec equal to one with params {x:1}.

Normalisation also applies inside nested attribute objects, i.e. map values whose only keys are 'id' (a non-empty string), 'params' (a map) and optionally 'format' (a string), including such maps inside lists: their parameters lose default values, and an emptied 'params' entry is removed, so {attribute:{id:'sum', format:'duration', params:{distinct:false}}} becomes {attribute:{id:'sum', format:'duration'}}. Ordinary nested maps that are not attribute objects are not normalised: {o:{a:false}} stays as is.

getParamsMap() never returns null (empty map when there are no parameters). When the spec was made by a public constructor and no normalisation was needed, the map and its nested lists and maps are unmodifiable (put throws UnsupportedOperationException). When normalisation changed the map, or the spec came from AttributeSpecBuilder or replaceParams, the returned map is a plain modifiable map and modifying it changes the spec's equality (as the original does).
getParams() returns a SpecParams view of the parameter map, created on first call; repeated calls return the same instance.

is(String) is true exactly when the ID equals the argument (false for null); is(ValueFormat) is true when the format equals the argument, i.e. has the same format ID; is(String, ValueFormat) requires both. Example: a spec 'foo' in TEXT gives is('foo') true, is(TEXT) true, is('foo', HTML) false.

as(format) returns this same instance when the spec's format equals the given one (by format ID), otherwise a new spec with the same ID and parameters and the given format. Example: 'foo' with params {x:1} in TEXT, as(HTML), has toString 'foo:{"x":1}:html'.

withParam(name, value) returns a new spec with the parameter set (replacing an existing value, appended at the end otherwise); the original spec is unchanged. A null value returns an equal spec with the parameters unchanged; a value that normalises away (e.g. false) removes the parameter. An AttributeSpec value is stored as a nested object {id, format, params} where params is present only if the spec has parameters. An invalid value type throws IllegalArgumentException, and a null name with a non-null value throws IllegalArgumentException ('null key is not allowed').

replaceParams(map) returns a new spec with the same ID and format whose parameters are the given map, only normalised: the map is neither copied nor validated. Null values are silently dropped by normalisation (instead of being rejected), values of unsupported types are accepted, a null map means no parameters, and if no normalisation is needed the spec keeps the caller's very map, so later changes to it show through the spec (as the original does).
noParams() returns a new spec with the same ID and format and empty parameters; it equals new AttributeSpec(id, format).

Two specs are equal when their formats are equal (same format ID, regardless of value class), their IDs are equal and their parameter maps are equal (map equality, so the order of keys does not matter). hashCode is consistent with equals and computed from ID, format and parameters. A spec is never equal to null or to objects of other classes.

toString() is the ID, then, if there are parameters, ':' and the parameters serialised as compact JSON in the map's iteration order, then ':' and the format ID. Examples: 'priority:priority', 'foo:{"x":1}:text', 'c:{"k":"a\"b","n":[1,2]}:text'. The text is computed once and cached. If the parameters cannot be serialised to JSON (possible only via replaceParams with an unsupported value) the JSON part is empty, giving e.g. 'foo::text'.

create() gives a builder with no ID, no format and no parameter builder; create(id) sets only the ID; create(id, format) sets both (either may be null); create(id, format, params) also copies the map into the parameter builder, ignoring a null or empty map; create(spec) copies the spec's ID, format and parameters, and create(null spec) is an empty builder. new AttributeSpecBuilder() equals create().

build() creates the spec with the same ID and format rules as the AttributeSpec constructors: a missing or blank ID throws IllegalArgumentException 'attribute id must not be empty' and a missing format throws 'attribute format must not be null'. The builder remains usable, and specs built earlier are not affected by later changes to the builder.

The built spec's parameters keep the builder's insertion order, leave out nested objects that are empty (recursively: an object containing only empty objects is dropped too), and are normalised like AttributeSpec parameters (false, Long 0, Integer defaults, empty lists dropped). Example: set a=1, set f=false, object o with k=v, an empty object e and list l=[1,2] give toString 'x:{"a":1,"o":{"k":"v"},"l":[1,2]}:text'.

params() creates the top-level parameter builder on first call and returns the same instance afterwards; its done() returns the owning AttributeSpecBuilder, and ParamsBuilder.build() is the same as calling build() on the owner.
setFormat returns the same builder instance retyped to the new format's value type, and setId returns the same instance; both overwrite earlier values.

Builders are equal when ID, format and parameter builders are equal; a builder whose params() was called but left empty is not equal to one where it was never called, although both build equal specs. toString is "AttributeSpecBuilder('<id>', <format id>, <params>)" with 'null' for unset parts and the params in map text form, e.g. "AttributeSpecBuilder('x', text, null)" or "AttributeSpecBuilder('sum', text, {attribute={id=timespent, format=duration}, distinct=true})".

AttributeSpecBuilder.ParamsBuilder.set(key, value) ignores a null value entirely (even with a null key, nothing is thrown); stores an AttributeSpec value as a nested attribute object; stores a Map value as a nested object builder holding a validated copy (an empty map is ignored); stores a List by reference after validation, so later changes to that list show in specs built later and in specs already built (as the original does); stores other valid scalars as is; overwrites an existing key keeping its original position. An invalid value throws IllegalArgumentException, e.g. 'invalid value type: java.lang.Object' or, inside a list, 'invalid list: invalid value at index 0: ...'; a null key with a non-null value throws IllegalArgumentException 'null key is not allowed'.

AttributeSpecBuilder.ParamsBuilder.object(key) returns the nested parameter builder stored under the key if there is one (so repeated calls return the same builder and add to it), otherwise creates an empty nested builder that replaces any scalar value under that key. Its done() returns the enclosing parameter builder. A null key throws IllegalArgumentException.
AttributeSpecBuilder.ParamsBuilder.remove(key) removes the entry (scalar or nested object) under the key, does nothing for a missing key, and returns the same builder.

AttributeSpecBuilder.ParamsBuilder.setAttribute(key, spec) stores, under the key, a nested object with 'id' = the spec's ID, 'format' = its format ID and, only if the spec has parameters, 'params' = a copy of them; it merges into a nested object already under that key (existing entries stay first). setAttribute(spec) uses the key 'attribute'. A null spec throws NullPointerException. Example: setAttribute(KEY) on an object already holding extra=1 gives {extra:1, id:'key', format:'text'}.

AttributeSpecBuilder.ParamsBuilder.copyFrom(map) does nothing for null or empty; otherwise validates the whole map first (a null value gives IllegalArgumentException 'invalid map: invalid value for key a: null value', a non-string key 'invalid map: non-string key ...') and then adds every entry as set would, nested maps becoming nested object builders, overwriting existing keys.

AttributeSpecBuilder.ParamsBuilder instances are equal when their content maps are equal, hash by content, and toString gives the content in map text form, e.g. '{z=3, a=2}' after setting z=1, a=2, z=3.

normalizeParams(id, map) returns the very same map instance when no entry needs to change (no default-valued entries at top level, and no nested attribute object, at any depth through lists and attribute objects, needing changes). It does not validate or copy values.

When anything needs to change, normalizeParams returns a new modifiable map in the original key order without the dropped entries (null, false, Long 0, empty list or map, Integer equal to the per-attribute default); all list values are copied into new lists and every nested attribute object anywhere in it is rebuilt with keys in the order id, format (only if present), params (only if non-empty after normalisation). Example: for id 'aggregation-parent', {depth:-1, level:0, other:-1} becomes {level:0, other:-1}.

A map is treated as a nested attribute object only if every key is 'id', 'params' or 'format', 'id' is a non-empty string, 'params' is a map, and 'format' is absent or a string; anything else (extra keys, missing params, empty id) is treated as an ordinary map and left untouched.

ofNullable(null) returns the same shared instance as undefined(); ofNullable(x) and of(x) return a defined value holding x. undefined(), error(), absent() and inaccessible() each return a shared singleton (same instance on every call). of(null) fails with AssertionError when Java assertions are enabled and returns undefined() when they are disabled.

A defined value has isDefined() true and isError(), isAbsent(), isInaccessible() false. All four undefined kinds have isDefined() false; isError() is true only for error(), isAbsent() only for absent(), isInaccessible() only for inaccessible(); plain undefined() has all three false.

getValue() returns the held object for a defined value and null for every undefined kind. getDefinedValue() returns the held object, and throws StructureRuntimeException with message 'unexpected undefined value' for any undefined value.

ifPresent(consumer) calls the consumer once with the held object for a defined value and does not call it for an undefined value; it returns the same instance in both cases. A null consumer causes NullPointerException on a defined value but is ignored on an undefined one.

toString() of a defined value is String.valueOf of the held object (e.g. 'x'); undefined kinds print '<?>' (undefined), '<!>' (error), '<->' (absent) and '<#>' (inaccessible). A value carrying loader data appends ' (+)', e.g. 'x (+)' or '<!> (+)'.

Defined values without loader data are equal when their held objects are equal (of(1) equals of(1), but not of(1L)), with hashCode equal to the held object's hashCode. Undefined values without loader data are equal when of the same kind. A value with loader data equals only another value with loader data of the same content and equal loader data; it is never equal to the same value without loader data (in either direction). Values of different kinds are never equal.

withData(data) returns a value of the same kind and content carrying the data, replacing any existing loader data. withData(null) returns the same instance when there is no loader data, and when there is some returns a new value without it, equal to (but, for undefined kinds, not the same instance as) the plain singleton. The original is never modified.

getLoaderData(cls) returns the attached loader data cast to cls if it is an instance of cls, null otherwise, and null when no data is attached. Example: of('x').withData(5) gives 5 for Integer.class, null for String.class.

cast(spec) returns this same instance when the held value is null (any undefined kind) or is an instance of the spec format's value class. On a mismatch, e.g. of(5).cast(spec in TEXT), it throws AssertionError (message: the value's text, a space, the spec's text, e.g. '5 key:text') when assertions are enabled, and returns null when they are disabled.

An implementation that overrides only receiveValues gets defaults where isCancelled() returns false and valuesReady, receiveMeta and receiveInaccessibleRows do nothing (no exception for any argument).

When the plugin loads values for a receiver it calls receiveValues on the loading thread with an attribute and a column of values for requested rows, possibly several times per attribute; it polls isCancelled() and stops loading quietly when it returns true; it reports rows the user may not see through receiveInaccessibleRows before delivering values, and calls receiveMeta once at the end of a successful load.

The constructor stores its six arguments without copying or null checks; getForest(), getRequestedRows(), getRequestedAttributes(), getValues(), getForestVersion() and getItemsVersion() return the same instances that were passed.

ConsistentRowValues.EMPTY has an empty forest, an empty requested-rows list, an empty attribute collection, getValues() the same instance as RowValues.EMPTY, and both versions equal to DataVersion.ZERO.
ConsistentRowValues does not override equals, hashCode or toString (identity semantics).

CoreAttributeSpecs constants have these IDs and formats (toString in brackets): PRIORITY [priority:priority], PROJECT [project:project], ASSIGNEE [assignee:user], REPORTER [reporter:user], CREATOR [creator:user], ISSUETYPE [type:issuetype], STATUS [status:status], ITEM [item:any], DUEDATE [duedate:time], CREATED [created:time], UPDATED [updated:time]; none has parameters. It also inherits all SharedAttributeSpecs constants, e.g. CoreAttributeSpecs.TOTAL_TIME_SPENT is the same spec.

CoreAttributeSpecs.Format holds PRIORITY (ID 'priority', value class Jira Priority), PROJECT ('project', Project), USER ('user', ApplicationUser), ISSUETYPE ('issuetype', IssueType) and STATUS ('status', Status). Because formats compare by ID only, CoreAttributeSpecs.PROJECT (format 'project') is not equal to SharedAttributeSpecs.PROJECT_ID (ID 'project', format 'id').

CoreAttributeSpecs.Id adds ITEM='item', CREATOR='creator', DUEDATE='duedate', CREATED='created', UPDATED='updated', COMPONENTS='components', AFFECTS_VERSIONS='versions', FIX_VERSIONS='fixVersions', LABELS='labels' and inherits the SharedAttributeSpecs.Id constants (e.g. CoreAttributeSpecs.Id.SUMMARY is 'summary'). CoreAttributeSpecs, its Format and Id classes have private constructors.
ItemValues.EMPTY returns null from getLoadedValue, getAttributeValue and get for every key and attribute, including nulls, and isOutdated returns true for every key and attribute.
LoadedValue.of(AttributeValue) returns a loaded value with getValue() the given instance and isOutdated() false; a null argument throws NullPointerException.
LoadedValue.of(T value) wraps AttributeValue.ofNullable(value): for null, getValue() is the undefined() singleton; isOutdated() is false.

Loaded values made by the factories are equal when their attribute values are equal (LoadedValue.of('x') equals LoadedValue.of(AttributeValue.of('x'))); hashCode is 31 plus the attribute value's hashCode (151 for 'x'); toString is the attribute value's toString.

For an implementation of getLoadedValue only: getAttributeValue(k, a) returns null when getLoadedValue returns null, else its getValue(); get(k, a) returns null when there is no loaded value or it is undefined, else the held object; isOutdated(k, a) returns true when there is no loaded value, else the loaded value's isOutdated(). Keys and attributes, including nulls, are passed through to getLoadedValue unchanged.
RowValues.EMPTY returns null from getLoadedValue, getAttributeValue, get(Long, ...) and get(long, ...) for any row and attribute, isOutdated is true for every row, and consume(f) never calls f.
The default get(long row, spec) boxes the row and returns the same as the generic get(Long, spec), i.e. it is based on getLoadedValue for that boxed row.
The constructor stores the values and checker as given (nulls allowed, no copying); getRowValues() and getUpdateChecker() return the same instances. No equals, hashCode or toString override.

SharedAttributeSpecs constants (toString in brackets): ID [id:id], KEY [key:text], SUMMARY [summary:text], DESCRIPTION [description:html], URL [url:text], ICON [icon:html], DISPLAYABLE_TEXT [displayable:text], DONE [done:boolean], EDITABLE [editable:boolean], PROJECT_ID [project:id], ISSUETYPE_ID [issuetype:id], STATUS_ID [status:id], VOTES [votes:number], WATCHES [watches:number], TIME_SPENT [timespent:duration], ORIGINAL_ESTIMATE [timeoriginalestimate:duration], REMAINING_ESTIMATE [timeestimate:duration].

TOTAL_TIME_SPENT, TOTAL_ORIGINAL_ESTIMATE and TOTAL_REMAINING_ESTIMATE are specs with ID 'sum', format DURATION and parameters, in this order, attribute = {id: the wrapped spec's ID, format: 'duration'} and distinct = true. toString of TOTAL_TIME_SPENT is 'sum:{"attribute":{"id":"timespent","format":"duration"},"distinct":true}:duration'; the others use 'timeoriginalestimate' and 'timeestimate'.

SharedAttributeSpecs.Id has DISPLAYABLE='displayable', PRIORITY='priority', PROJECT='project', USER='user', ASSIGNEE='assignee', REPORTER='reporter', TYPE='type', ISSUETYPE='issuetype', STATUS='status', SUMMARY='summary', DESCRIPTION='description', URL='url', KEY='key', DONE='done', EDITABLE='editable', VOTES='votes', WATCHES='watches', PROGRESS='progress', SUM='sum', ICON='icon'. SharedAttributeSpecs.Param has DISTINCT='distinct', ATTRIBUTE='attribute', ID='id', PARAMS='params', FORMAT='format', CHILDREN='children', LEAVES='leaves', STRICT='strict', SUBTREE='subtree', ANCESTORS='ancestors', TYPE='type', PRECEDING='preceding', LEVELS='levels', BASE_LEVEL='baseLevel'. The class and both nested classes have protected constructors.

The default loadAttributeValues(spec, rows, attrs, receiver) calls the five-argument form with strict=false; the default getAttributeValues(spec, rows, attrs) calls the five-argument form with strict=false and a null meta consumer; the default getConsistentAttributeValues(spec, rowsFn, attrs) calls the four-argument form with strict=false. Results and exceptions pass through unchanged.

In the plugin's implementation the getAttributeValues variants return the RowValues.EMPTY instance when the forest (or spec), the rows or the attributes argument is null; getItemValues returns ItemValues.EMPTY when either collection is null or empty; getConsistentAttributeValues returns ConsistentRowValues.EMPTY when the spec or the attributes are null; isItemAttribute(null) is false.

In the plugin's implementation getItemValues loads each distinct item (duplicates in the input are loaded once) as a top-level row of a temporary flat forest and returns values looked up by item identity.

In the plugin's implementation getConsistentAttributeValues reloads until the forest and item versions did not change during loading, at most the number of attempts set by the setting structure.attribute.maxConsistentLoadAttempts (default 5), then throws StructureException; the result's forest, rows and versions are the ones the values were computed for.
ValueColumn.empty() returns a column whose getValue returns null for every key, including null.

The constructor throws IllegalArgumentException when the ID is null, empty or blank ('format id must not be empty'), longer than 190 characters ('format id must not be longer than 190 chars'), contains a colon ('format id must not contain colon'), or when the class is null ('format class must be not null').

Standard formats and their (ID, value class): HTML (html, String), TEXT (text, String), ID (id, String), NUMBER (number, Number), BOOLEAN (boolean, Boolean), TIME (time, Long), DURATION (duration, Long), JSON_OBJECT (json, Map), JSON_ARRAY (jsonArray, List), ANY (any, Object), ORDER (order, Comparable). getFormatId() and getValueClass() return the constructor arguments.
Formats are equal when their format IDs are equal, regardless of value class (new ValueFormat('text', Integer.class) equals TEXT); hashCode is the format ID's hashCode; toString is the format ID.

getStandardFormat(id) returns the standard constant instance for 'html', 'text', 'number', 'boolean', 'duration', 'time', 'json', 'jsonArray', 'order', 'id' or 'any' (case-sensitive: 'TEXT' gives null), and null for null or any other ID such as 'user'.

cast(spec) returns the same spec instance when its format equals this format (by ID), otherwise throws ClassCastException with message 'cannot cast attribute <spec> as format <format id>', e.g. 'cannot cast attribute key:text as format html'.

In the plugin's implementation a subscription reports its window: getForest() returns the current forest spec (an empty text-query forest when none was set), getAttributes() the attributes in the order added as an unmodifiable collection, and getRows() the rows sorted ascending without duplicates.

In the plugin's implementation getUpdate(version) returns a full update with all current values when the version is null, DataVersion.ZERO, from another subscription or older than the kept history; an empty incremental update when nothing changed since that version; otherwise an incremental update with the changed values. The update's version is the one to pass next time. getUpdate does not start loading.

In the plugin's implementation loadValues() starts background loading and returns a future completed with the data version when loading finishes, already completed when there are no attributes; isLoadingValues() is true while such loading runs. getFullUpdate(timeout, unit) starts loading, waits and returns all window values, throwing TimeoutException when it does not finish in time; getFullUpdate() wraps interruption, timeout and cancellation into StructureRuntimeException.

In the plugin's implementation drainAttributeErrors() returns the loading errors collected since the previous call and forgets them, so an immediate second call returns an empty collection; it never returns null.
The constructor stores the version, full flag and values; getVersion() returns the given version, isFull() the flag and getValues() the given values instance (null accepted).
isEmpty() is true exactly when the values are the RowValues.EMPTY instance (identity), independent of the full flag; another RowValues with no values, or null, gives false.
AuthContext.Custom(user, flag) returns exactly the given user (null allowed) from getUser() and the given flag from isSecurityOverridden(); these and sudo are final.
AuthContext.Custom.sudo(f) runs f through StructureAuth.sudo with the context's user and flag, returning f's result and propagating its exception unchanged.

AuthContext.CURRENT reads the thread's state at each call: getUser() returns StructureAuth.getUser() and isSecurityOverridden() returns StructureAuth.isSecurityOverridden(); its sudo(f) simply calls f in the current context, returning its result and propagating its exception, without changing user or flag.

StructureAuth.getUser() returns the user of the innermost active sudo on this thread (null for anonymous), or, outside any sudo, the user logged in to Jira's authentication context; if that context is unavailable it returns null and logs an error only once. getUserKey() is the Jira key of getUser(), null for anonymous.
StructureAuth.isSecurityOverridden() is false outside any sudo and inside sudo returns the flag of the innermost active sudo.

StructureAuth.sudo(user, flag, f): if user equals Jira's current logged-in user and flag equals the current override flag, f just runs. Otherwise, during f, getUser() returns user, isSecurityOverridden() returns flag and Jira's authentication context reports user as logged in; afterwards, even if f throws, the previous sudo state (or none) and Jira's previous logged-in user are restored. f's result is returned and its exception propagates unchanged. Nested calls restore the outer state.
The one-argument StructureAuth.sudo(f) runs f as the current getUser() with security override on.

StructureAuth.currentContext() returns a new AuthContext.Custom with the user and override flag in effect at the time of the call (outside sudo: Jira's logged-in user and false), unaffected by later changes on the thread.

PARAM_INCLUDE_DASHBOARD_GADGETS is 'includeDashboardGadgets'. The default backup(writer, ids, params) ignores the params and calls backup(writer, ids) with the same writer and ids (null ids passed through). The default migrate(reader, MigrationMapping, reporter) calls the deprecated migrate(reader, map, reporter) with mapping.getStructureIds() and the same reader and reporter.
The default clearUserStructureCachesOnAllNodes(ApplicationUser) calls clearUserStructureCachesOnAllNodes(String) with user.getKey(); a null user causes NullPointerException.

In the plugin's implementation clearCurrentUserStructureCaches() clears the user-specific caches of StructureAuth.getUser() on this node and does nothing (logs a message) for anonymous; the all-nodes variants act locally and send a cluster message so other nodes do the same; on a node receiving a user-key message, nothing happens if no user has that key.

The default clear(ApplicationUser) calls clear(String) with user.getKey(); a null user causes NullPointerException. ForestAccessCache.UserLookupException is a checked exception with a no-argument constructor.

In the plugin's implementation clear(null user key) does nothing; getInvisibleRows returns an empty set for null or empty input and otherwise the subset of the given rows (duplicates ignored) whose items the user may not see, including rows that do not exist; checks that cannot be made count as invisible.

Every getter first reads the Jira application property of that name; if it is null or empty, the JVM system property of the same name is used; otherwise the default. When Jira's application properties cannot be reached (for example outside Jira), getApplicationProperty logs a warning and returns null, so the system property decides.

getLong(name, d) and getInteger(name, d): a non-empty application property is parsed as a plain decimal number, and an unparsable one gives d without looking at the system property. Otherwise the system property is decoded as Long.getLong / Integer.getInteger do, so hexadecimal ('0x10' gives 16) and octal ('010' gives 8) forms are accepted, and an unparsable or missing value gives d (e.g. 'abc' gives d).

getBoolean(name, d): a non-empty application property gives Boolean.parseBoolean of it (true only for 'true' ignoring case, so 'yes' gives false even when d is true); otherwise a set system property gives Boolean.parseBoolean of it ('TRUE' gives true, 'yes' gives false); otherwise d. getBoolean(name) is getBoolean(name, false).

getProperty(name, d) returns the non-empty application property, otherwise System.getProperty(name, d); a system property set to the empty string is returned as the empty string. getProperty(name) is getProperty(name, null), returning null when nothing is set.
